sentences.text: The genus Jianchangornis is known from a single species, Jianchangornis microdonta, which preserves a skull, partial skeleton, and feathers.
This subadult individual measured 33 cm in length, stood 26 cm tall at the hip, and had a mass of 1.2 kg.
Zhou and colleagues formally described the genus in 2009, noting that Jianchangornis microdonta is the only known species.
It belongs to the class Reptilia and is part of the parent group Ornithuromorpha, making it a basal ornithuromorph dinosaur.
Fossils were discovered in the Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning, China, dating to the Aptian stage between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
